newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy fin min Visco sees no major 1997 mini-budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy fin min Visco sees no major 1997 mini-budget.

text.p: Italy, which has recently had to roll out large mid-year mini-budgets to make up for shortfalls in the full budget, might not have to present any corrective measures in 1997, the Italian Finance Minister said.
If it does, they will only be of limited scope, Vincenzo Visco told the lower house of parliament's budget committee.
The government last month unveiled a budget which is designed to slicee 62.5 trillion lire off next year's deficit -- double the size of the originally planned package.
"This will limit to the full, if not render superfluous a mini-budget for next year," Visco said.

Turning to a new regional tax introduced in the budget, Visco said it would save companies some two to three trillion lire thanks to a cut in the overall number of taxes payable combined with an simplification of the fiscal system.
Visco said earlier this month that the tax would weigh heavily on large corporates, making it more difficult for firms to avoid tax demands by moving money abroad.
The lower house budget committee will continue examining the package but has to finish work on the bill by October 28. The draft law will then go for debate to the full lower chamber.
Six lower chamber commissions have so far approved the budget -- the finance, culture, constitutional affairs, foreign affairs, defence and justice commissions.
All lower house commissions, which are examining aspects of the budget relating to their areas of legislation, have until the end of today to express an opinion. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
